question: Which mroute state is created when Bidirectional PIM is deployed at a site?
explanation:
Bidirectional PIM is a different flavor of multicast than what you are probably used to (sparse, dense and sparse-dense mode). Most multicast networks have a couple of sources and many receivers. Bidirectional PIM has been invented for networks where we have many sources and receivers talking to each other. An example of this is videoconferencing where it's not just 1 source with many listeners but all the participants are communicating with each other.
The downside of using PIM sparse mode with many active sources and receivers is that we will see many mroute state entries that can take quite some resources.
Using PIM sparse mode the RP builds 2 entries: (*,G) and (S,G).
When we use PIM bidirectional mode the RP will never build a (S,G) entry and we only allow the (*,G) entry for the shared tree. PIM routers will never build the SPT (Shortest Path Tree) towards the source.
theory: Bidirectional PIM builds only a shared (*, G) tree rooted at the RP and never builds source-specific (S, G) state, unlike sparse mode which maintains both. This is intentional: Bidir is designed for many-to-many applications (e.g., trading, video conferencing) where building an (S, G) entry per source would not scale, so traffic simply flows toward/away from the RP along the shared tree without ever forming a shortest-path tree. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 1 — PIM Bidirectional Mode)
